notes.text: Mexican mortgage credit is dominated by the public housing funds: in the year to March 2024 Infonavit and Fovissste originated 76.2% of home-purchase loans by number and 50.2% by value, while most commercial bank mortgages are peso-denominated at fixed rates, averaging 10.4% with a 19-year term. Infonavit lends at rates adjusted to the worker's income rather than tracking the policy rate, so Banco de México's moves reach borrowers slowly and mainly through new bank lending.

sources.title: Indicadores Básicos de Créditos a la Vivienda, datos a marzo de 2024

notes.text: The federal Vivienda para el Bienestar programme aims to build 1.8 million homes over the 2024 to 2030 term, with Infonavit, Conavi (500,000 homes) and Fovissste (100,000) as delivery agencies and eligibility focused on households earning under two minimum wages. Direct state construction of low-cost units adds supply at the bottom of the market, where the price index has been rising fastest.

sources.title: Vivienda para el Bienestar: Hay 274 mil en construcción en el país; el programa atiende a cerca de 7 millones de personas

notes.text: As of June 2026 about 274,000 programme homes were under construction nationwide, including 191,368 Infonavit homes, with Conavi expecting its first 50,000 completions by end-2026. Much of this pipeline has yet to be delivered, so its effect on prices lies ahead rather than in current data.

sources.title: Vivienda para el Bienestar: Hay 274 mil en construcción en el país; el programa atiende a cerca de 7 millones de personas

notes.text: The SHF House Price Index, published quarterly by Sociedad Hipotecaria Federal, covers homes bought with a mortgage, with breakdowns for new and existing homes, all 32 states, 74 municipalities and eight metropolitan zones. Because it covers only mortgage-financed purchases it omits cash sales; in the first quarter of 2026 economic-social housing rose faster (11%) than mid-range and residential homes (7.5%).
